name: Elise Cotton
life: “I still remember printing a sign too large for the window.” People around the corner outside Coastal Barber know Elise by a small Tuesday habit. Elise usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I wrote the notice in tiny type to save paper. I want one copy I can read myself from a driver's seat.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. Elise has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears. Elise leans a shoulder against the wall during long conversations during a conversation.
personality: Elise tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Elise will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
agenda: To print one sign a working driver can actually read.
family: Nia Oak is Elise’s stepsibling. Elise can always ask for five minutes alone. Nia asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The borrowed bass*, Nia says, “I usually have to tell bands to turn down. I loaned this one the quiet side of the fountain for the phone call.”
connections: Sam Sloan (route planner). They redesign the printed diversion around the users it left out.

reactions.response: Elise checks with the intended recipient before leaving a late parcel.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Elise stays where the child can see the shop door and asks the neighboring counter to help find the adult expected there.

reactions.situation: If a relative makes a joke at a child's expense
reactions.response: Elise repeats the child's actual point and waits for a reply to that.
